monument_name: Gaṇeśa Mandira at Dau Bāhāḥ (1870s CE)
description_en: Facing towards the south, the Gaṇeśa Mandira is situated at the north-east corner of Dau Bāhāḥ Nani. It is a syncretic mixture of two building types dedicated to Gaṇeśa. The temple stands on a five-bayedphalcā. Eight of the columns date back to ca.1870. It seems, thus, that thephalcāwas built long before the temple, which then was constructed on top of it. An iron fence is supported by wooden pillars at the eastern, southern, and western sides of the temple, and an iron channel gate provides the entrance into the temple. Inside the outer temple structure is a smaller temple attached to the back wall. Inside the niche of the temple is an image of Gaṇeśa, the main deity of the temple. Gaṇeśa is sitting insukhāsanaon top of two mice, holding an axe andmodakawith their left hands. One of the right hands is inabhayaposture, and another one is holdingakṣamālā. Above the image is atoraṇamade of copper plate, upon which the images are embossed. On the top-centre of thetoraṇais an image of Garuḍa, under which there is an image of Gaṇeśa standing inālīḍhaposture. On either side of Gaṇeśa one can see Ṛddhi and Siddhi. Small niches can be found in the wall of the temple, with statues of Sarasvatī, Nārāyaṇa, Lakṣmī, and Bhīmasena. Moreover, there are three stone inscriptions attached to the wall. One of the inscriptions informs that the temple was built in 1901 by Jīta Govinda Amātya and his family. Thetoraṇawas donated by the Amatya family in 2004, and the marble floor was donated in 2016.Three of the sides of thephalcāare open, but the northern wall is attached to a private house. 8 wooden pillars and 14ṭuḍālassupport the roof of the outer temple. The roof is made of tiles and fashioned in a pagoda style. A pinnacle with twojvalānhāykãson either side of it tops the roof. To enter thephalcā, one must ascend three stairs flanked by two statues of sitting lions. Close to each lion are images of two moles, although the head of the mole on the eastern side is broken. In front of thephalcāare two concrete pillars supporting a beam with a hanging bell. In the middle of the beam is ajvalānhāykã, and on either side of this are statues of a mole. To the east of the bell stands an oil-lamp balustrade.
description_ne: यो गणेश फल्चा दौबहाननिको ईशान कोणमा अवस्थित छ । पूर्वाभिमुख फल्चाको बीच भागमा शिखर शैलीको सानो shrineमा गणेश मूर्ति स्थापित छ । फल्चा भित्र रहेको गणेश shrine बनाई गजूर चढाउने कार्य सन् १९०४ मा जीत गोविन्द अमात्य र उनका परिवारले गरेका थिए (स्रोत : अभिलेख) । यस गणेशलाई  स्थानीयले  स्थानगणेशको रूपमा पुज्ने गर्छन् । फल्चाको गारोसँगै टाँसेर तीन वटा शिलालेख राखिएका छन् । तीमध्ये एउटा शिलालेखबाट प्राप्त जानकारी अनुसार यो shrine १९०१ मा जीत गोविनद अमात्य र उनका परिवारद्वारा बनाइएको हो ।यस  फल्चा  ८  वटा थामो माथि उभिएको छ  । यसको  तीनतर्फी भाग कुनै संरचनाले छोएको छैन  भने उत्तरी भागले व्यक्तिगत भवनमा छोएको छ । फल्चाको छानो पेगोडा शैलीमा छ । छानोको  मध्य भागमा गजूर छ र गजुरको दायाँ–बायाँ ज्वालान्हाय्कंहरू पनि  राखिएका छन् ।  फल्चामा  प्रवेश  गर्न  तीन तहको सिंढी बनाइएको छ । सिंढीको दायाँबायाँ एकजोडा सिंह र मुसा राखिएका छन् । फल्चाको अगाडी सिमेन्टको थामो रबीममा झुण्डिएको घण्टा  चढाइएको छ । उक्त घण्टा नजिकै १२ तह  भएको दियोको गुच्छा बनाईएको छ । फल्चामा खुल्ला आवत—जावत गर्न नमिल्ने गरी फलामे ढोका  रबारहाली घेरिएको छ । फल्चाको भित्तामा साना–साना खोपीहरू (niches) बनाई तिनमा सरस्वती, नारायण, लक्ष्मी, भीमसेन आदिका मूर्तिहरु राखिएका छन्  ।  सोही भित्तामा तीनवटा अभिलेखहरू पनि टाँसिएका छन् ।
monument_assessment: Good (very few light surface damages, renovated or repaired)
references: Sources and references Sources Inscription from VS 1958

historical_events.event_description: The temple was constructed by Jit Govinda Amātya, Hari Govinda Amātya, Kirti Govinda Amātya and their family.
Statues of sitting lions were installed on each side of the main entrance. They were donated by Amṛta Vajracārya.
Installation of a group of 12 rows of stepped oil-lamps by Tulasī Bahādura Śreṣṭha
Renovation of the monument by the Dau Bāhāla Ṭola Sudhāra Samiti.
A bell was offered to Gaṇeśa by Bhuvana Maṅgala Jośī and Jyāpu Jośī.
